text: Whisper: "This is a wave. I can love the part of me that feels it."
section: Grounding Menu: Choose One or Two Things > Breath
reader: someone mid-trip, or the person helping them, picking one breathing option to calm a panicking body

sentences.payoff: they have a short phrase to whisper with the slow breath, naming the panic as a wave that passes
sentences.follows: the last of the breath options, after the counts and the warnings

sentences.s: I can love the part of me that feels it."
sentences.payoff: they turn toward the part that feels the panic with love while the breath slows, the guide's method for fear, instead of only waiting it out
sentences.follows: the second half of the same whisper
sentences.link: none: it is the second sentence of the same whispered line, so nothing needs to tie it to the first

placement: the Breath list's last line, after the counts and the breath-hold warning; it is the line the reader says while breathing

opens.why_reading: it gives the reader the words to say while they breathe, which is what they reach this line for

same_point: none: read the Breath list from its label to Music for these points; only this line gives words to say, and For the Person Helping has "I can love the part of me that feels it." in the helper's self-talk

needed.reader: a fresh Haiku agent given tools/humanization/needed_read_brief.md with the paragraph, its heading and what it is for (NEEDED-READ.raw.md beside this receipt, item 2)
unneeded: I can love the part of me that feels it."

they turn toward the panicking part of themselves with love while the breath slows, the guide's method for fear (Demons: "Love removes hooks"), which "This is a wave." alone leaves out; it is why the line is added (his METHOD-WHERE answer, round 28)

questions.Q1: PASS: the whisper is the line's point and comes first

questions.Q4: PASS: no term a reader wouldn't know
questions.Q5: PASS: two sentences of one whisper
questions.Q6: PASS: the wave first, then what to do with the feeling

questions.Q8: PASS: a thing to say while breathing, in the Breath list

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
